summary: A simple expense tracker that records daily expenses, sets a daily budget, and provides statistical summaries.
requirements: Record an expense with amount, category, optional description, and date.
List expenses with optional date-range filtering.
Get and set the daily budget limit.
Retrieve statistical data: total spent today, remaining budget today, total spent this month, and breakdown by category.
assumptions: Dates are stored as ISO 8601 dates (YYYY-MM-DD) without time.
Amounts are positive numbers with up to two decimal places.
SQLite is sufficient for the expected data volume.
open_questions: Should the app support multiple users or authentication in the future?
Should expense deletion be soft-delete or hard-delete?

tasks.title: Design database schema and implement expense CRUD operations
tasks.description: Create SQLite tables: expenses(id, amount, category, description, date) and budget(id, daily_limit). Implement DAO functions for creating, listing (with optional start_date/end_date filters), deleting expenses, and getting/setting budget.
acceptance_checks: HTTP POST /api/expenses with valid payload returns 201 and created expense.
HTTP GET /api/expenses returns 200 with array of expense objects.
HTTP DELETE /api/expenses/{id} returns 204 when exists, 404 when not found.
HTTP GET /api/budget returns 200 with {daily_limit}.
HTTP POST /api/budget with valid daily_limit returns 200 updated budget.

tasks.title: Implement statistics endpoint
tasks.description: Add route GET /api/stats that computes total spent today, remaining budget today (daily_limit - total_today), total spent this month, and sum of amounts grouped by category. Returns JSON with those fields.
acceptance_checks: With no expenses, GET /api/stats returns 200 with totals zero and empty by_category array.
After inserting known expenses, returned totals match manual calculation.
Response includes daily_budget_limit from budget table.

tasks.title: Set up React project with API service layer
tasks.description: Initialize Vite + React + TypeScript project. Create a singleton service (expenseApi.ts) wrapping fetch calls to the backend endpoints (list, create, delete, get/set budget, stats). Include basic error handling and TypeScript types matching API schemas.
acceptance_checks: Service file compiles without errors.
Each exported function returns a Promise that resolves to the expected TypeScript type.
Mock server responses show correct URL and method calls.

tasks.title: Build ExpenseList component with form and delete button
tasks.description: Component shows a table/list of expenses fetched on mount via listExpenses (optionally filtered by date). Includes a form to submit new expense (amount, category, date, description). On submit calls createExpense and refreshes list. Each row displays a delete button calling deleteExpense. Shows loading/error states.
acceptance_checks: Rendering component displays empty list initially.
Submitting valid form adds a new row without page reload.
Delete button removes the row and updates list.
Form validation prevents submission of non-positive amount or empty category.
Error states shown when API returns non-2xx.

tasks.title: Build Budget component to set and display daily budget
tasks.description: Component fetches current budget via getBudget on mount. Shows input field to set new budget; on submit calls setBudget and updates displayed limit. Includes validation (positive number).
acceptance_checks: Component loads and displays current budget (default 0).
Entering a valid number and clicking Save updates the displayed value without reload.
Submitting invalid or non-positive number shows error and does not call API.
API error responses are shown to user.

tasks.title: Build Stats component to display statistical data
tasks.description: Component calls getStats on mount and displays: total spent today, remaining budget today, total spent this month, and a bar chart (or list) of spending by category. Handles loading and error states.
acceptance_checks: On mount with no data shows zeros and empty category list.
After adding expenses via ExpenseList, stats update accordingly (can trigger via refetch or prop).
Values match calculations from backend (verified by manual test).
Error states shown on non-2xx responses.

risks: Backend uses SQLite which may have concurrency limits if multiple users later added – plan to migrate to PostgreSQL if scaling needed.
Frontend state management relies on prop drilling or useContext; as app grows, consider adopting Redux or Zustand for scalability.
No authentication means data is exposed to anyone who can reach the API; if multi-user support is required, add JWT-based auth.
Date handling assumes client and server share same timezone; storing ISO date strings without time may cause off‑by‑one errors across zones – consider storing UTC timestamps.
Statistics endpoint performs aggregates on every request; with large datasets this could become slow – consider adding indexes on expense.date and caching.
